title: Before you sell in the Northern Territory
description: What to get ready before you list an NT property. Summarised from NT.GOV.AU pages.

sources.title: Buying or selling property with pools or spas

items.title: Engage a conveyancer or property lawyer
Have your conveyancer prepare the NT approved contract of sale
items.detail: Agents can only use a form approved by the Registrar or the Law Society Northern Territory.

items.title: List the chattels and any fixtures you want to exclude from the sale
Request your building file from Building Advisory Services (bas.files@nt.gov.au, $7 per lot)
If any work was never approved, ask a registered building certifier about a certificate of existence
If there's a pool, get a compliance certificate in your name using the NT pool compliance certificate application, or an acknowledgement notice using the NT pool declaration of compliance
If there's no pool, ask your conveyancer whether you need to sign the NT vendor no-pool statutory declaration
For a unit, give your conveyancer the body corporate manager's details and gather the by-laws, AGM minutes and levy notices
If tenanted, give 24 hours' notice for each viewing
Plan for the buyer's 4 business day cooling-off period (none at auction)
Tell your lender you are selling
